events.title: Three Hezbollah operatives who were planning to launch drones at troops in southern Lebanon were killed in drone strikes yesterday, the military says. The IDF says troops of the Givati Brigade identified the operatives in an area north of the Litani River, and a short while later, the Israeli Air Force "eliminated the terrorists with precise attacks while they tried to escape from the area." The Givati soldiers also located a weapons depot, containing rockets and explosive-laden FPV drones, the army says. The arms cache was then destroyed in a strike, the IDF adds.

events.summary_en: Delivery of the Supreme Leader's message to the families of the Minab school martyrs. Ayatollah Vakilpour, Special Representative of the Supreme Leader of the Revolution, during a trip to eastern Hormuzgan, met and held talks with the families of the martyrs of the Shajarat Tayyibah school in Minab. During this meeting, the message and greetings of the Supreme Leader of the Revolution were conveyed to the families of the great martyrs, and their patience, steadfastness and sacrifice were praised. The families of the martyrs also, in a cordial atmosphere, shared their memories and moral characteristics of their martyr children, as well as their concerns, demands and views with the Supreme Leader's representative.

events.title: An IDF soldier was killed and three others were wounded in a Hezbollah drone attack in southern Lebanon overnight, the military announces. The slain soldier is named as Staff Sgt. Adam Tzarfati, 20, of the Commando Brigade's Maglan Unit, from Rosh Haayin. At around 1 a.m., a explosive-laden first-person view drone launched by Hezbollah struck a site in the southern Lebanon town of Yohmor, near the Beaufort Castle, where Israeli troops were operating. The blast killed Tzarfati and wounded another soldier seriously. Two other troops were lightly hurt in the attack, the army says. The wounded soldiers were airlifted to a hospital and their families were notified, the IDF adds.

events.title: Three Hamas weapon depots in the Gaza Strip were struck last week to "remove a threat" to Israeli troops, the military says. According to the IDF, the facilities were used to store explosive devices, assault rifles, sniper rifles, and other equipment. At one site, 10 pickup trucks used by Hamas were destroyed, the military says. "The weapons were intended to be used against IDF troops operating in the area of the Yellow Line and Israeli civilians," the IDF says, adding that the weapons were destroyed "to remove the threat."
